races.title: State Senate, District 13
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Lisa Grafstein
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina Senate District 13 since 2023. Civil rights and employment lawyer since 1995. Ran her own Raleigh firm for 16 years, then became litigation counsel at Disability Rights North Carolina. Served on the NC State Personnel Commission 2010–2013.

endorsements.text: Her campaign site lists endorsements from Lillian's List, Equality North Carolina, the Police Benevolent Association, States Win, Sierra Club, NCAE, Planned Parenthood and the NC AFL-CIO.
Ballotpedia lists Sierra Club North Carolina and States Win among her 2026 endorsements, along with several Sway voting groups.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was raised. We found no recorded stance from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, guns, or refusing donor money. We found no legislation she sponsored that we could confirm, and no reporting on controversies. The environment and law enforcement sections of her campaign issues page were cut off, so anything she says there is not included. Her statement on investor home-buying is general and cites no bill. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys.

local.label: Roots 55: She was born in Amityville, New York in 1966, and her campaign site says she has lived in Wake County since 1990, after finishing college in 1988. That makes her an adult arrival more than 25 years ago.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since January 2023. Civil rights and employment lawyer since 1995, with 16 years running her own firm. Litigation counsel at Disability Rights North Carolina from 2011. Served on the NC State Personnel Commission 2010–2013.
qual.why: Prior legislative service combined with a long law career fits the high range for writing law and the budget. Committee seats and nonprofit boards were not counted.
qual.label: Prior legislative service combined with a long law career fits the high range for writing law and the budget. Committee seats and nonprofit boards were not counted.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Her campaign site says investment firms buying up single-family homes prices out first-time buyers, and that the state can discourage use of housing stock as an investment vehicle. It names no specific bill.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says 'We will have a healthier and more equitable community when we protect the right to abortion and reproductive freedom.'

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says the state should increase pay for teachers. It does not address vouchers or charters, and it criticizes cuts to public school funding.

cands.name: Robert van Brederode
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 13 in 2026. His campaign site says he is a law professor. No prior elected office is documented in the pages reviewed.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Robert van Brederode was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We could not find his employer, his years as a law professor, or any other career details. His campaign site gives general statements about liberty, small government and common sense, but nothing specific on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or schools. We found no documented actions in office, no land-use or development stances, no controversies and no foreign ties. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him, and he did not complete its candidate survey.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: His campaign site says he is a law professor and that he is entering politics for the first time. Ballotpedia lists no prior office.
qual.why: His campaign site says he is a law professor, but no page gives his employer, years of work or any policy, budget or legislative role. A score would be a guess, so it is left blank.
